evidence.note: Orientation phase: inspect data/template, check compute, calibrate bytes-per-token and CE/bpb target, confirm shards — establishes the problem frame before any build.

Build then explicit correctness gates BEFORE scaling: 'Smoke test param count and roundtrip' (quant/dequant load path) and 'Verify smaller ckpt size' (the <32MB budget gate) — size and roundtrip correctness locked prior to the full run.
Dedicated compute-milestone: short runs to measure step time and check compilers before committing to the full training run — sequencing capacity/compute as a checked step.

Full run launched only after gates; then 'Verify checkpoint contract and OOD probe' and 'Eval dequantized model on full val' — a post-training contract/forward done-check (notably deferred to after the first scaled run rather than fully locked before).

Improvement milestones with fallback: 'backup current ckpt' / 'Backup 0.967 ckpt, launch longer run' — preserves known-good before each targeted improvement attempt, showing frontier/fallback thinking but only along the train-longer axis.

reasoning: The agent shows clearly ordered phases each with a concrete done-check — smoke-test param-count+roundtrip and size verification locked before the full run, step-time measured, baseline val_bpb established, contract/dequant verified, then improvement runs that preserve a fallback checkpoint — which exceeds the level-5 anchor's 'rough success criteria'. It falls short of a clean 8 because the full grader-interface/forward contract check was performed after the first scaled run rather than before scaling, and short of 10 because the capacity↔size↔compute tradeoff is managed only partially explicitly (mainly train-longer with a preserved backup), so I place it at 7 between the 5 and 8 anchors.
